messages:
Maya Su: Heads-up — BlueFork Logistics reported an outgoing wire was returned by the correspondent with reason 'BIC mismatch'. Funds landed back on our float. They attached an MT103 copy. Reassigning to payments.

wire-bot: Payment ID 0x9f3d auto-flagged: RETURN_REASON=INVALID_INTERMEDIARY_BIC | return_code=R02

Owen Li (Payments): Can you paste the MT103 snippet + the original SWIFT/BIC they submitted? Need to see which field failed (beneficiary vs intermediary).

Maya Su: Paste from the customer MT103 (redacted):
```
20:REFERENCE12345
50K:/ACCT/123456789
59:/BEN/BLUEFORK LTD
70:Invoice 4382
52A:BFORKUS33
57A:INTLGB2LXXX
```
They claim 57A was `INTLGB2LXXX` (no trailing digit). Our return says intermediary bank rejected BIC.

Juno Park - Finance: Looks like the correct correspondent for the beneficiary bank should be `INTLGB22XXX` (two-digit branch ID), not `INTLGB2LXXX`. That L vs 2 looks like a transcription error.

Eli Ramos (Ops): Checked payment transform pipeline logs for 0x9f3d — we normalize BICs by stripping non-alphanumerics and uppercasing, but we don't validate against SWIFT registry. Log snippet: `transform: prop=intermediary_bic value=INTLGB2LXXX | normalized=INTLGB2LXXX | validated=false`.

Owen Li (Payments): So bad input + no validation = correspondent rejected. Two actions: (1) refund/return reconciliation to customer, (2) re-initiate with corrected BIC if they confirm. I'll own.

Maya Su: Customer says they copied BIC from their ERP export; they can confirm full BIC and beneficiary address. They've also asked if we can auto-detect likely typos.

Juno Park - Finance: For now, refund instructions: reverse to their settlement account and tag with original ref. Also add a note to their invoice indicating wire failed due to intermediary BIC mismatch (for their AR/AP team).

Owen Li (Payments): I'll kick off the refund to clearing account now and open a case with operations to add a validation warning on BIC format (and optional SWIFT lookup). ETA for refund: <24h. I'll follow up here once done. :thumbsup:

Eli Ramos (Ops): Quick temporary mitigation: adding a regex check that BIC must be 8 or 11 chars and log a `validation_warning` if the last 3 chars look non-numeric when expected. I'll deploy a light rule to staging and roll to prod tomorrow.

Maya Su: Copy — I've messaged the customer asking for corrected MT103 and beneficiary address.

Owen Li (Payments): Assigning to me: I'll also check if our UI trims any trailing characters when customers paste in the dashboard field (possible cause). If so, we'll patch.

wire-bot: Case 0x9f3d status updated -> REFUND_INITIATED by Owen Li (Payments).

Maya Su: Thanks team. Will update the customer once refund completes.

Owen Li (Payments): Update — refund confirmed queued, expected settlement within 1 business day. Will reopen if any issue. :white_check_mark:
